CONTEXT: aigate is a Go CLI "verification gate". It decides whether an AI-made change broke or weakened checks: it checks out a fixed BASE commit and the HEAD commit in isolated git worktrees, runs the configured checks (pytest / go test -json / vitest with JUnit) on both, normalizes results into test-id -> status maps, and applies invariant rules (every id passed at base must exist and pass at head; skips, missing ids, protected-file line removals, and new files on approval_on_add globs are flagged). Config .aigate.yml is read from the BASE commit. Verdict priority: verification_incomplete > check_weakened > behavior_failure > ok.

Read: docs/02-DESIGN-gate.md (spec: sections 3-5 and 8), internal/rules/rules.go, internal/gate/gate.go, internal/gate/exec.go, internal/gitx/gitx.go, internal/adapter/*.go (junit.go, gotestjson.go, preset.go, exitcode.go), internal/runner/runner.go, internal/config/config.go, internal/report/report.go, cmd/aigate/cli.go, and the e2e scenarios e2e/builder.go, e2e/scenarios_py_test.go, e2e/scenarios_go_test.go, e2e/scenarios_ts_test.go (they show the toy projects and the .aigate.yml used for each stack: Python protects tests/**, pytest.ini, pyproject.toml, .aigate.yml and approval_on_add **/conftest.py, **/testutils/**, **/fixtures/**; Go protects **/*_test.go, go.mod; TS protects **/*.test.ts, vitest.config.*, package.json, package-lock.json).

THREAT MODEL: an AI coding agent can edit, add, delete or rename ANY file in the repository's HEAD commit (and its working tree), but cannot touch the BASE commit, the aigate binary, ~/.aigate (approvals and ledger), or the user's terminal/environment variables. Its goal: get a WEAKENED, INCOMPLETE or BROKEN change (production behaviour wrong, or tests neutralized) to be judged `ok` by `aigate run` (and then pass `aigate check`).

TASK: List the 12 most promising concrete bypasses, ranked by plausibility (most plausible first). For EACH give:
1. Name.
2. Stack(s) it applies to: pytest, go test, vitest (one or more).
3. Exact file edits (paths and the essential code/lines added/changed/removed), concrete enough to reproduce.

5. Whether you think it is fixable in the gate with a small sound change (and what change), or inherent to a v1 invariant gate.
Prefer attacks that survive the existing rules; skip attacks the code clearly already catches unless the catch is fragile. End with a 3-line summary of the weakest point.
